title: FinovateFall 2026: Everything You Need to Know
summary: FinovateFall 2026 runs Sept 9-11 at the Marriott Marquis Times Square, NYC. Demo format, agenda, compliance sessions, costs and how to prepare.
body_markdown:
**TL;DR:** FinovateFall 2026 runs September 9-11 at the Marriott Marquis Times Square in New York, built around 70-plus live fintech demos of seven minutes each with no slide decks allowed. Risk and compliance is one of four official 2026 innovation pillars, and roughly two in three attendees hold executive titles. For compliance buyers, the demo format is the draw: it compresses vendor evaluation that normally takes weeks of scheduled calls into a single afternoon.


## The essentials


FinovateFall is run by Informa Connect and has been operating for close to twenty years. Its defining constraint is the demo format — seven minutes, live product, no slides — which forces vendors to show working software instead of describing a roadmap.


Detail Information


Dates September 9-11, 2026


Venue Marriott Marquis Times Square, New York


Format 70+ live seven-minute demos, no slide decks, plus keynotes, power panels, expert debates and workshops across three stages


Audience Roughly 2 in 3 attendees are executives; banks of all sizes, credit unions, fintechs, VCs, solution providers


Cost Tiered pricing that rose after August 21; free Leadership program places for qualifying directors, heads, SVPs and C-level staff at financial institutions


Accreditation CPD certified, with credits provided in accordance with NASBA


The Leadership program is the most underused part of the pricing structure. Directors, heads of function, SVPs and C-level staff at financial institutions can qualify for complimentary places, and eligible banking leaders also get access to Leaders+, a pre-event insights session and drinks reception. Anyone at a bank or credit union with a senior title should check eligibility before paying full price.


## Who actually attends


FinovateFall draws a buyer-heavy audience, which is unusual for a fintech event and is the main reason it is worth a compliance leader's time. Attendees come from all ten of the largest US banks, plus national, international, regional and community banks, credit unions, wealth managers, venture investors, fintech operators and technology providers. Two in three hold executive titles.


The event runs two curated sessions that shape who is genuinely reachable. The Community Bank Spotlight is restricted to community bank executives and selected fintechs, and the Credit Union Spotlight works the same way for credit unions. Both are peer discussions paired with vetted technology, which solves a real problem: a community bank BSA officer at a general fintech conference usually spends the day being sold enterprise platforms priced for a different institution.


The practical composition matters when planning meetings. This is a room where a compliance leader can meet peers at similar institutions and the vendors serving them in the same two days. It is less useful for meeting regulators or law enforcement, who are largely absent — that is what an anti-financial-crime conference is for.


## What's on the agenda


Compliance attendees will spend most of their time on the CX and Trust stage.


FinovateFall organizes its 2026 programme around four innovation pillars: AI-powered operations, payments and cross-border solutions, digital experience and security, and risk and compliance. Content runs across three dedicated stages.


The AI & Innovation stage covers agentic commerce, banking operating systems, copilots, scaling and hands-on workshops. The CX & Trust stage carries compliance, financial crime, customer-centric banking and personalization. The Future of Money stage covers lending, payments, small business banking and stablecoins. A compliance attendee will spend most of their time on CX & Trust, with selective trips to AI & Innovation.


The[published agenda](https://informaconnect.com/finovatefall/agenda/2/) has a clear financial crime thread. Day one includes a special address on AI agents in financial services and another introducing an agentic workbench for banks, featuring Jeremiah Sadow, Executive Director of Group Financial Crimes Compliance at Lyzr AI. Day two closes with a quick-fire keynote from Jennifer White, Senior Director of Global Banking and Payments Intelligence at J.D. Power, on responding to fraud when the attacker has better tools than the defender, followed immediately by a power panel on managing financial crime risk with advanced technologies. That panel brings together Jas Randhawa of StrategyBRIX, Andrew Endicott of Gilgamesh Ventures, Allison Watson of Plaid and Azba Habib, Chief Compliance Officer at Column Bank.


Day three features a power panel on trust, risk and financial crime in a digital world, with Daniel Latimore of RFI Global, Katherine Avery of Chimayo Consulting, Shanthi Shanmugam of Casap and Bernadette Smith, Chief Customer and Banking Officer at Starling Bank. The day also includes a fireside chat with a former US regulator on the changing regulatory landscape, featuring Finovate's David Penn and Syed Raza of FTI Consulting.


## Sessions worth prioritizing


The demo sessions are the reason to attend, and they should anchor the schedule rather than fill gaps between panels. Several demo rounds specifically cover fraud prevention, dispute resolution, authentication and identity verification, and regulatory compliance. Seven minutes of live software tells a buyer more about whether a product exists than a sixty-minute sales call.


Among the content sessions, the day two pairing is the highest-value block of the event for a compliance audience — the J.D. Power fraud keynote followed by the financial crime risk panel, with a sitting bank Chief Compliance Officer on stage. The[Best of Show awards](https://finovate.com/finovatefall-2026-agenda-revealed/) follow at the end of day two during the drinks reception, which is a useful shortcut to the demos that the wider audience found most convincing.


The day three fireside chat with a former regulator is worth staying for. Practitioner panels describe what institutions are doing; former regulators describe what supervisors are looking at, and the two do not always line up.


One scheduling trap to note: IMPACT Funders & Founders runs alongside the main event on September 11, and access is *not* included with a FinovateFall pass. It is a separate event connecting startups and scaleups with investors. Anyone expecting to walk in with a conference badge will be turned away.


Attendees planning to evaluate compliance tooling may find it useful to review the current landscape of[compliance automation platforms](https://sphinxhq.com/blog-posts/best-compliance-automation-platforms-fintech-2026) beforehand, so the demos land against a mental model rather than creating one from scratch.


## How to prepare


Check Leadership program eligibility first. If a free senior place is available, that changes the budget conversation entirely, and the Leaders+ reception is a better networking environment than the main floor.


Use the ConnectMe networking app before travelling. Finovate structures the event so that pre-booked meetings drive most of the value, and the vendors worth meeting fill their calendars early. Arriving with a diary already populated is the single highest-return preparation step.


Read the demo company list in advance and shortlist eight to ten to watch closely. With more than seventy demos across multiple parallel sessions, the difference between a productive event and a blur is deciding beforehand which problems to shop for. Write down the two or three specific gaps in the current stack — alert backlog, onboarding turnaround, document verification, dispute handling — and match demos to them.


Book accommodation early. The Marriott Marquis hosts the event, and staying in the venue removes the commute entirely in a part of Manhattan where that is worth something. Exclusive rates are available through the event.


Finally, if the institution is a community bank or credit union, confirm Spotlight eligibility. Those sessions are the most efficient hours of the conference for smaller institutions, and they are capped.


## How to evaluate vendors on the floor


FinovateFall is a buying event, and the demo format already filters out vendors with nothing working to show. That still leaves the harder questions, which no seven-minute demo can answer. Given that global spending on AML and know-your-customer compliance runs to roughly $304 billion a year according to research by Ronald F. Pol cited by FinTech Global, the diligence is worth the awkwardness. These questions are worth asking at every stand.


That last question is particularly useful at a conference where the top ten US banks are in the room. A platform proven at a $500 billion institution may be badly matched to a $2 billion community bank, and the fastest way to find out is to ask for a reference at a comparable size.


Sphinx sits on top of the systems an institution already runs, automating the analyst work that follows an alert while keeping every decision documented and reviewable.


## What to do after


Demo-heavy conferences produce a specific failure mode: a long list of interesting products and no decisions. The antidote is to rank the shortlist against the gaps written down beforehand, within a week, and to kill anything that does not map to one of them.


For the two or three that survive, request a technical session with the actual implementation team rather than a follow-up with sales. Seven minutes of demo plus a booth conversation is enough to establish that a product is real and roughly what it does. It is not enough to establish whether it fits, and the people who can answer that are usually not the ones on the floor.


CPD credits are provided after the conference in accordance with NASBA and require a request, so anyone who needs them should submit that promptly rather than assuming they arrive automatically.


For teams deciding how to spend the rest of the season's travel budget, the[fall 2026 financial crime and compliance conference calendar](https://sphinxhq.com/blog-posts/financial-crime-compliance-conferences-fall-2026) compares FinovateFall against the other major options, including the events that serve compliance buyers more narrowly. Institutions weighing whether automation is the right answer to a growing alert queue may also want to work through[the AML efficiency gap](https://sphinxhq.com/blog-posts/how-to-close-the-aml-efficiency-gap) before signing anything.


## Frequently Asked Questions


### When and where is FinovateFall 2026?


September 9-11, 2026, at the Marriott Marquis Times Square in New York. The event is organized by Informa Connect and runs across three stages, with the separate IMPACT Funders & Founders event taking place alongside it on September 11.


### What makes the FinovateFall demo format different?


Demos are seven minutes long, live, and slide decks are not permitted. More than seventy companies demo across the event, hand-picked for market readiness rather than concept. The format means attendees see working software rather than a roadmap presentation, which compresses early-stage vendor evaluation considerably.


### How much does FinovateFall cost?


Pricing is tiered and rose after August 21, 2026, with savings of up to $400 available before that date. Directors, heads of function, SVPs and C-level staff at financial institutions may qualify for complimentary places through the Leadership program, and Finovate runs a Community Partnership Program offering free passes to members of qualifying non-profits, community banks and credit unions.


### Is FinovateFall useful for compliance and financial crime teams?


Yes. Risk and compliance is one of the four 2026 innovation pillars, the CX & Trust stage carries dedicated compliance and financial crime programming, and multiple demo rounds cover fraud prevention, identity verification and regulatory compliance tooling. It is a buying and benchmarking event rather than a regulatory one — there is little regulator or law enforcement presence compared with a dedicated anti-financial-crime conference.


### Is IMPACT Funders & Founders included in a FinovateFall pass?


No. IMPACT Funders & Founders is a separate event running alongside FinovateFall on September 11, focused on connecting startups and scaleups with investors. Access requires its own registration and is not covered by a FinovateFall pass.
